Maintenance Report — MNT-0035-005

Asset: WELL-0035 (SW-23 Well 035, T200, Southwest Block 23) Equipment: flowline Work started: 04 Aug 2023 08:00 · Finished: 04 Aug 2023 18:00 · Well stopped for this job: 10 hours Crew lead: Daniel Foster (U-302) · Crew: Brian Coleman, Kevin Price · Contractor: Tumbleweed Flowline Co. Triggered by: inspection INS-0035-0041 on 2023-08-03 Report written: 05 Aug 2023

What happened

The weekly drone inspection INS-0035-0041 at 13:45 on 2023-08-03 found crude oil on the pad: about 8.0% of the pad area, estimated 3.7 bbl. The inspector noted: "Pooled fluid near flowline." The field operator shut the well in, closed the flowline valve and placed earth berms and absorbent pads. The release was contained about 7.8 hours after the inspection. The crew traced the leak to a threaded coupling on the flowline close to the wellhead.

Root cause

Corrosion under a failed protective wrap on the coupling.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 3 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).
  • Hot work permit issued for welding; gas test before welding read 1% LEL, below the 10% limit (WS-04).

Work done

  1. Excavated around the coupling.

  3. Welded in new pipe and a new fitting.
  4. Coated the new joints.
  5. Excavated the stained soil.
  6. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Testing and return to service

Maintenance Report — MNT-0035-027

What happened

Field staff reported that the electric motor driving the pump jack had stopped and would not restart. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0035-0187 showed the wellhead at 33.4 °C with the air at 33.9 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. An insulation test showed a winding fault, so the motor was replaced with an exchange unit. The well stayed shut in for about 6 days longer than the repair itself because the crew was committed to a higher-priority spill response elsewhere in the field.

Root cause

Winding breakdown from heat and age.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Disconnected and removed the motor.
  2. Fitted the exchange motor on the existing base.
  3. Aligned the sheaves and tensioned the belts.
  4. Checked rotation direction and motor current.

Summary of the fix: replaced the electric motor with an exchange unit.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 2 hours; motor current within the nameplate rating and stroke rate normal. The well was returned to production.
